glosses: To level to rise in one part of a body of water, especially a shallow one, because of a storm surge caused by persistent wind.

examples.text: The level set up at the south end of the lake after a day of north winds.

glosses: To provide the money or other support that someone needs for an important task or activity.

examples.text: Winning the lottery has set them up for life.

glosses: To establish someone in a business or position.

glosses: To trick or lure (someone) in order to entrap them.

examples.text: They claimed that they weren't selling drugs, but that they'd been set up by the police.

glosses: To make (someone) proud or conceited (often in passive).

examples.text: M. Robespierre looked at me sideways and smiled and said to Madame, ‘You're a young lady after my own heart.’ This set her up for the day.

glosses: To matchmake; to arrange a date between two people.

examples.text: Just past the hour Agbonlahor set up the second, crossing for Bent to net.

glosses: To deceive an opponent and capitalize on their reactions with a certain technique or maneuver.

examples.text: When you make an opening you merely cause an opponent to uncover a target somewhere on his person. But when you set up an opponent, you knock him off balance with one punch so that he should be an open target for a following punch. Unless he's knocked off balance, he's not set up.
